code: fit <- glm(asthma ~ no2 + sex + maternal_smoking + maternal_age,            family = binomial, data = foresty_cohort)  overall <- foresty_main(list(fit), exposure = "no2",                         labels = c(no2 = "NO2")) by_sex <- foresty_interaction(fit, exposure = "no2", interaction = "sex") by_smoking <- foresty_interaction(fit, exposure = "no2",                                   interaction = "maternal_smoking")  foresty_combine(Overall = overall, Sex = by_sex,                 `Maternal smoking` = by_smoking)   # In the layout of a journal, the interaction p-value written once against # each block, and without the numbers beside the plot. foresty_combine(overall, by_sex, by_smoking, layout = "jama")  foresty_combine(overall, by_sex, by_smoking, table = FALSE)   # Every block drawn alike, the overall estimate included. foresty_combine(Overall = overall, Sex = by_sex, emphasize = NULL)   # Two exposures are two figures, one apiece, named for them. fit_bc <- glm(asthma ~ black_carbon + sex + maternal_smoking + maternal_age,               family = binomial, data = foresty_cohort) figures <- foresty_combine(   Overall = foresty_main(list(fit, fit_bc),                          exposure = c(NO2 = "no2",                                       `Black carbon` = "black_carbon")),   Sex = by_sex,   `Black carbon by sex` = foresty_interaction(fit_bc, "black_carbon", "sex") ) names(figures) #> [1] "NO2"          "Black carbon" figures[["NO2"]]

title: foresty 0.0.1
text: First release.

title: foresty 0.0.1
text: foresty_app() provides Shiny interface interactively selecting exposures, modifiers, contrasts, colours, plot layouts. foresty_main() creates forest plots exposure effects fitted models. foresty_interaction() estimates exposure effects within levels modifier, tests interaction, displays results forest plot. foresty_combine() combines overall subgroup results single forest plot. Supports glm(), lm(), survival models, lme4 models, robust cluster-robust standard errors sandwich. Supports categorical continuous exposures, including spline terms contrasts specified exposure values. Effects can reported per specified increments per interquartile range using contrast. Interaction tests can use Wald, likelihood ratio, tests. GEE quasi-likelihood models use Wald test. Results returned ggplot2 objects can customized standard ggplot2 syntax. Forest plot layouts can customized foresty_layout(), predefined styles including "classic", "jama", "nejm", "lancet", "bmj", "revman". foresty_report() html argument provide self-contained HTML reports containing model results, interaction tests, coefficient tables, forest plots. Results can exported PNG SVG figures .rds objects. summary(), .data.frame(), broom::tidy(), broom::glance(), coef(), vcov(), predict(), formula(), nobs() supported foresty results.
